beats.title: Stamp Act Protests in the Colonies
beats.description: Crowds in colonial port towns hanged effigies and menaced tax collectors to force the repeal of a new tax on printed paper.

beats.title: Boston Tea Party
beats.description: Colonists disguised as Mohawk men dumped a ship's chests of tea into Boston harbour to protest taxation without representation.

beats.title: Women's March on Versailles
beats.description: Thousands of Parisian women, angry at bread prices, marched to the royal palace and brought the king back to the capital.

beats.title: Spa Fields Reform Meeting
beats.description: Thousands gathered in a London field to hear a radical orator and agree a petition to the Prince Regent for reform.
beats.note: First meeting 15 Nov 1816; riot at the second on 2 Dec.

beats.title: Peterloo
beats.description: A huge peaceful rally in Manchester demanding parliamentary reform was charged by cavalry, leaving many dead and hundreds injured.

beats.title: Reform Rally at Newhall Hill
beats.description: Vast crowds gathered outside Birmingham to press Parliament to pass the Reform Bill, a model for mass political meetings.
beats.note: Year of the largest Newhall Hill meeting; earlier meetings were held in 1830-31.

beats.title: Chartists Rally at Kennington
beats.description: Chartists gathered south of the Thames before marching a giant petition for the vote to Parliament, only to be turned back.

beats.title: Hyde Park Sunday Trading Protests
beats.description: Tens of thousands of Londoners jeered the aristocracy's carriages in the park to oppose a bill banning Sunday trading.

beats.title: Hyde Park Railings Torn Down
beats.description: Reform League supporters, barred from the park, pushed over its iron railings and held their meeting for the vote anyway.

beats.title: Great Franchise Demonstration
beats.description: Tens of thousands of trade unionists processed through London to a park rally backing a bill to widen the vote.

beats.title: Bloody Sunday in Trafalgar Square
beats.description: Unemployed workers and radicals marching on London's central square were broken up by police and soldiers.

beats.title: Coxey's Army Marches on Washington
beats.description: Jobless men led by an Ohio businessman marched to the capital to demand public works jobs during an economic depression.

beats.title: St Petersburg Petition March
beats.description: Workers led by a priest walked to the Winter Palace to petition the tsar and were fired upon by troops.

beats.title: Women's Sunday Rally in Hyde Park
beats.description: Suffragettes converged on the park from seven London platforms in one of the largest rallies for votes for women.

beats.title: Suffrage Parade in Washington
beats.description: Thousands of women marched down Pennsylvania Avenue for the vote on the eve of a presidential inauguration, facing hostile crowds.

beats.title: Petrograd Women's Day Protest
beats.description: Women textile workers took to the streets for bread and peace, and the unrest grew into the fall of the tsar.
beats.note: Protests began on International Women's Day.

beats.title: First National Hunger March
beats.description: Unemployed men from across Britain walked to London to demand work and relief, starting a tradition of long marches.

beats.title: Sacco and Vanzetti Protests
beats.description: Demonstrations in cities across the world demanded clemency for two Italian-born anarchists facing execution in Massachusetts.

beats.title: Bonus Army Marches on Washington
beats.description: Thousands of jobless First World War veterans camped in the capital to demand early payment of their service bonuses.

beats.title: Jarrow March
beats.description: Two hundred unemployed shipyard men walked from a northern English town to London carrying a petition for work.

beats.title: Rosenstrasse Protest in Berlin
beats.description: Non-Jewish wives gathered outside a Berlin building for days until their detained Jewish husbands were released.

beats.title: Bengali Language Movement Protests
beats.description: Students in Dhaka defied a ban on assemblies to demand official status for their mother tongue, and police fired on them.

beats.title: First Aldermaston March
beats.description: Campaigners walked for four days from London to a nuclear weapons research site, debuting the peace symbol.

beats.title: Anpo Protests in Japan
beats.description: Huge crowds surrounded the parliament in Tokyo to oppose a revised security treaty with the United States.

beats.title: May Events in Paris
beats.description: Student barricades in the Latin Quarter spread into a nationwide wave of protest against the government and old order.

beats.title: Stonewall Uprising
beats.description: Patrons and neighbours of a New York bar fought back against a police raid, igniting the modern gay rights movement.

beats.title: First Earth Day
beats.description: Some twenty million Americans joined rallies and teach-ins for the environment across the country.

beats.title: Greenham Common Women's March
beats.description: Women walked from Wales to a Berkshire airbase and set up a peace camp against cruise missiles.

beats.title: People Power Revolution in Manila
beats.description: Millions filled a Manila highway and stood in front of tanks until a long-ruling president fled the country.

beats.title: Tiananmen Square Protests
beats.description: Students and workers occupied Beijing's central square for weeks to demand reform until the army cleared it.

beats.title: Defence of the Moscow White House
beats.description: Muscovites built barricades around the Russian parliament to resist a hardline coup against the Soviet leader.

beats.title: Battle of Seattle
beats.description: Tens of thousands blockaded a global trade summit, bringing the anti-globalisation movement to world attention.

beats.title: Global Anti-Iraq-War Protests
beats.description: Millions marched in hundreds of cities worldwide on one weekend in the largest coordinated demonstration in history.

beats.title: Orange Revolution in Kyiv
beats.description: Crowds in orange filled Independence Square for weeks until a rigged presidential election was annulled.

beats.title: Occupy Wall Street
beats.description: Protesters camped in a New York park against inequality under the slogan We are the 99 percent, inspiring camps worldwide.

beats.title: Hong Kong Umbrella Movement
beats.description: Demonstrators with umbrellas against pepper spray occupied main roads for weeks demanding free elections.

beats.title: Women's March
beats.description: Millions in Washington and cities across the world marched in pink hats the day after a presidential inauguration.

beats.title: Woman, Life, Freedom Protests
beats.description: The death of a young woman in police custody over a headscarf sparked nationwide street protests across her country.
